chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, from Ṣafwān, from Ibn Muskān, from Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who is in a state of taharah and trims his nails or his hair: must he repeat the wudu (ablution)? He said: No, but he should wipe his head and his nails with water. He said: I said: They claim that wudu (ablution) is required because of it. He said: If they dispute with you, then do not dispute with them, and say: This is the sunnah (prophetic tradition).

key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: the normative prophetic and Imamic practice

ai.seo_question: Does cutting hair or nails invalidate wudu (ablution) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on trimming hair or nails while already in a state of taharah. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that this does not require repeating wudu (ablution), though one may wipe the head and nails with water, and instructs the believers to respond by affirming that this is the sunnah (prophetic tradition).
